description:
Somos Viento Sur Lab,  del Colegio Provincial de Educación Secundaria N°14 "Pueblos Originarios" de Pico Truncado (Santa Cruz- Argentina). 

Nos atraen los nuevos desafíos y tenemos entusiasmo de superación. Nos apasionan la tecnología, la robótica y la Ciencia. Participamos en NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 con el desafío de diseñar y crear un juego o aplicación interactiva que permita a los estudiantes gestionar un puesto avanzado lunar o marciano.
summary:
The project is an online simulator game that aims to train Junior Astronauts, aged 7 to 12, by offering a realistic experience with decision-making challenges to survive at the SUN 214 space station located on Mars. The station has a clear and ambitious mission: to prove that the colony can become 100% self-sufficient.

The game introduces children to science and technology in a simple, accessible, and playful way. It makes learning fun through striking visuals that are both appealing and familiar to kids.
Using HTML, CSS, and Java software, combined with AI-assisted vibe coding, this simulator was created with two distinct game modes: a single-player mode (inspired by the popular game Among Us) and a role-based multiplayer mode. In this second mode, astronauts must work as a team, make decisions, and solve problems that affect the entire crew, allowing them to experience every situation in a vivid and hands-on way. As an extra challenge, the game also incorporates block-based programming mini-games and AI training focused on Machine Learning.
details:
It is the year 2040, and humanity has taken the ultimate leap forward. The NASA space agency has sent 5 astronauts to establish and test the first permanent colony on Mars, the SUN 214 Outpost.

The base is strategically located in Utopia Planitia, a vast plain in the northern hemisphere of Mars. This site was chosen because, back in 2016, the NASA radar instruments (SHARAD) discovered that a massive underground ice deposit lies beneath this region, covered only by a thin layer of Martian soil.

This game aims to train Junior Astronauts—cadets aged 7 to 12—to survive at the SUN 214 space station, which has a clear and ambitious mission: to prove that the colony can become 100% self-sufficient by producing its own water, air, food, and fuel using the ISRU methodology (In-Situ Resource Utilization). This means taking advantage of the planet's native materials instead of bringing them from Earth, without depending on expensive and infrequent shipment from earth.
